messages:
pranav: Quick follow-up from the hotstart RFC — I sketched a few concrete heuristics for safetensors verification + warmstart ordering we can try in staging. Wanted feedback before I turn this into a tiny PR.

maya: SGTM, can you list the failure modes you're trying to avoid?

pranav: Sure — mainly: silent corruption (bad shard byte ranges), long blocking verification on first request (latency spike), and cascade re-eviction when verification holds locks. Also trying to keep memory pressure predictable when we decompress/quantize on hotpath.

liam: +1 to avoiding head-of-line blocking. What's your thinking about doing probabilistic checksum sampling vs full-verify?

pranav: Proposal A: background full-verify after a lightweight header sanity check. Header check runs inline (magic, size, manifest ref), then we serve from mmap/read and let a background worker compute a 64-bit rolling checksum and compare to manifest. If mismatch, we mark the shard "tainted" and schedule a remap.

samantha: How do we expose "tainted" to the caller? Return 5xx or graceful fallback to a different model variant?

pranav: Default: graceful fallback to a compatible variant (quantized or smaller shard set) controlled by routing policy. We'll surface an error in tracing/console but not 5xx by default to keep running apps alive. For strict tenants we have a config flag to fail hard.

liam: Background verify is fine but can still overwhelm IO when many shards arrive concurrently. Suggest stagged concurrency + global verify rate limiter tied to prefetch budget.

pranav: Agreed — add a verify_concurrency token bucket shared across the node. If tokens exhausted, verification is queued with low priority. We also add a fast-sample path: if prefetched-bytes > X then do an immediate sample-hash of first/last 4KB to catch common corruption.

maya: What about quantized-on-load? We often want to memory-map float weights and re-quantize into a local slab. If verify runs after re-quant, we need to ensure checksum covers canonical-on-disk encoding, not in-memory transformed slab.

pranav: Exactly. Verification happens against on-disk bytes. Re-quant is an orthogonal transform; we'll record a provenance header in the hotcache: {"source_checksum":..., "transform":"q8_0"} so we can detect mismatch between cache and source.

samantha: Can we add a tiny example of header we expect in safetensors-sidecar/manifest? That will help infra and validators.

pranav: Yep. Draft header (pseudo):
```
{"magic": "safetensors-v1", "shard_index": 2, "bytes": 7340032, "sha64": "AbC...", "sample_hashes": ["0xdeadbeef","0xabad1dea"], "flags": ["gzip?","encrypted?"], "compatible_variants": ["q8_0","f16_packed"]}
```

liam: Nice. For encrypted shards we need to avoid doing decryption on inline path. Background verification should either decrypt lazily or handshake with KMS asynchronously. Risk is key access latency cascades into verify backlog.

pranav: Plan: for encrypted shards we mark verify status "pending-key" and kick an async KMS fetch which is also gated. If key fetch fails we fallback to variant routing. Permanent key failures produce an alert and mark the shard unusable.

devin: One more tradeoff: do we prefer index-first warmstart (load small header + index) or header-first? Index-first helps partial hotplug but complicates compatibility checks across formats.

pranav: My leaning: header-first for universal compatibility (single canonical file header), index may be sidecar. But we support index-first fastpath if the index contains provenance + sha64. That gives us an opt-in high-performance path.

maya: Telemetry we should capture: verify_latency, verify_queue_depth, sample_fail_rate, fallback_rate, memory_delta_during_requant. Also per-tenant strict_fail config metric.

liam: Add a metric for "hotstart_eviction_clash" — how often verification holds eviction locks and triggers eviction churn.

pranav: Good call. For rollout: feature-flag background-verify off by default, enable in staging with low concurrency, ship a small histogram dashboard, then ramp by region. I'll open a PR with the state machine and the header schema.

samantha: If you can, include a short test plan: simulate corrupted shards, delayed KMS, and a high-concurrency warmstart burst. Also unit test the provenance header roundtrip.

pranav: Will do. Any objections to me implementing the token-bucket limiter + sample-hash fastpath first?

liam: No objections. +1 from me.

maya: +1. Thanks — this reads actionable.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: please link PR to infra-config change for verify_concurrency default.

pranav: Noted. PR coming in a few hours.

devin: One last nit — make sure fallback routing preserves per-request latency SLO hints (so we don't route to a slower variant without informing the caller's SLO tracking).

pranav: Yep I'll wire an SLO hint header when fallback occurs: X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason + X-Redwood-SLO-Impact.

samantha: Great. I'm going to add a short blurb to the RFC doc linking this thread.

pranav: Thanks all.
